title: Pricing Basis for Price Adjustment Credits and Competitor Prices, Ridgeline Orders & Delivery
content:
When Ridgeline lowers its own price on an item ordered through Ridgeline Orders & Delivery within the program's price adjustment days after the order date, the difference is credited once per item as a price adjustment credit on the customer's request, provided the item has not been returned; clearance, open-box and special buy prices are excluded where the program excludes them. A competitor's lower price on the identical in-stock item is matched only before purchase, where the program matches competitor prices, and never by a credit after the order.

### Basis questions

**Whose lower price counts for a credit?**
Only Ridgeline's own lower price on the ordered item. A competitor's price is never credited after the order.

**Is the credit made without being asked?**
The rule grants it on the customer's request.

**How much is credited?**
The difference between the price on the order and Ridgeline's lowered price, once for the item. *Hypothetical figures:* an item ordered at $189.00 whose Ridgeline price drops to $159.00 within the period earns a price adjustment credit of $30.00. If the price later drops again, to $149.00, the item has already received its one credit.

**What if the item has gone back?**
An item that has been returned does not receive a price adjustment credit.

**Do clearance and similar prices count?**
Where the program excludes them, a clearance, open-box or special buy price is not a basis for the credit.

**And a competitor's lower price?**
It is matched before purchase only, on the identical in-stock item, where the program matches competitor prices.

### Conditions together

| Lower price is Ridgeline's own, within the period after the order date | Item not returned | Price is not an excluded clearance, open-box or special buy price | Customer requests it | Credit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | The difference, once for the item |
